notes: Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance on duty-type units (disclosure, explain-your-work, verify, syllabus-statement duties): one coder used require, the other permit or neutral; resolved by reserving require for AI use that is itself required, permit for conditions on permitted use, and neutral for procedural duties that take no position on AI use. (2) Actor and phase for principle and scope statements (all vs admin; general vs during-work/before-course): resolved by using all/general for principles and scope statements that bind no single role or time, and the addressee/time of the action otherwise. (3) policy_type: coders split between neighbouring types (P01/P06, P29/P30/P32, P47/P48, P56/P77, P04/P05); resolved from the source sentence, and two Appendix A categories and the 'syllabi must not specify sanctions' line went to UNCOVERED rather than a stretched fit. (4) Adjacent statements in one sentence were sometimes paired by the automatic alignment but are different statements (CTL syllabus, CTL guidance tier lines, EECS embedded-AI vs categories); these were split and counted as only_A/only_B and both kept. (5) All single-coder units were real policy statements and were kept; B found more granular list items (Ecampus guideline sub-items, COE sentences), A found a few EECS and CTL sentences. Document-level stance agreed in all 8 documents.
